Pinkeye Detection Pipeline (Step 1 + Step 2)

Project: Cattle Pinkeye Detection
Prepared for: Team update
Date: March 2026

1) Executive Summary

The project progressed from robust eye localization (Step 1) to multi-model disease classification on cropped eye regions (Step 2), with controlled augmentation experiments.

Main outcomes:

  • Step 1 eye detector achieved mAP50 = 0.995 on validation.
  • On the Step 2 baseline benchmark (5-fold CV), Strong CNN+Transformer had the best overall F1/accuracy balance.
  • Across augmentation ablations, ResNet18 became the most stable top performer under constrained augmentation settings.
  • The eye-only approach shows strong feasibility for pinkeye screening, with model choice and augmentation policy materially affecting minority-class performance.

2) Step 1: Eye Localization (YOLOv8)

Data and setup

  • Eye dataset for annotation: 117 images, single class (eye).
  • Annotation validation: 117/117 valid, no errors.
  • Split: train/val/test = 93 / 11 / 13.

Detector performance

  • Precision: 1.000
  • Recall: 0.999
  • mAP50: 0.995
  • mAP50-95: 0.631

Classification-dataset detection pass

  • Sample classification pool (data/sample_test): 408 images
  • Images with eye detections: 394
  • No detections: 14 (copied for manual review)

Conclusion: detector quality is strong enough to support the classification stage.

Eye detected by the model Cropped by the model

3) Step 2: Classification Benchmark (5-Fold Stratified CV)

Dataset

  • Cropped-eye dataset: 394 images
  • Healthy: 309
  • Pink-eye: 85

Protocol

  • 5-fold stratified CV
  • 5 epochs per fold
  • Weighted cross-entropy for imbalance handling
  • Early stopping enabled

4) Augmentation Experiments and Insights

A) with_aug vs no_color_aug

No-color setup used only flip + rotation + small Gaussian noise (no color jitter/affine).

Most important deltas (no_color_aug - with_aug):

  • ResNet18: improved
  • Delta F1_pinkeye: +0.0198
  • Delta Accuracy: +0.0076
  • EfficientNet-B0: decreased
  • Delta F1_pinkeye: -0.0279
  • Strong CNN+Transformer: decreased
  • Delta F1_pinkeye: -0.0379

Interpretation: color/affine augmentations appear beneficial for non-ResNet models in this dataset, while ResNet18 benefited from a simpler augmentation policy.

B) Gaussian-noise ablation (flip+rotation only)

Comparing flip+rotation to no_color_aug (which included Gaussian noise):

  • ResNet18: F1_pinkeye decreased (-0.0210)
  • EfficientNet-B0: F1_pinkeye decreased (-0.0202)
  • Strong CNN+Transformer: F1_pinkeye increased (+0.0117)

Interpretation: Gaussian noise acted as useful regularization for CNN baselines but hurt the strong hybrid model.

C) Minority-only augmentation (pink_eye only)

Applying flip+rotation only to minority class:

  • Best in this setting: ResNet18 (F1_pinkeye 0.9060 +- 0.0282)
  • Did not outperform each model's best previous setting overall.

Interpretation: minority-only augmentation alone was not a universal improvement.

5) Overall Technical Conclusions

  1. Eye-crop classification is viable: strong metrics across multiple architectures confirm informative signal exists in eye region.
  2. Model ranking depends on augmentation regime: - Baseline benchmark winner: Strong CNN+Transformer
    - Most robust under constrained/controlled augmentations: ResNet18
  3. Class imbalance handling is effective: weighted CE + stratified CV produced stable minority-class recall/F1.
  4. Augmentation policy is a first-order factor: small transform changes materially shift F1_pinkeye.

6) Next Stage: DDPM-Based Synthetic Data Augmentation

As the next stage, we are working on DDPM models to generate class-conditional synthetic eye images (healthy and pink_eye) for data augmentation.

Planned usage: - Generate synthetic images under controlled quality checks. - Add selected synthetic samples to training folds in a controlled manner. - Re-run the Step 2 classifier benchmarks and compare against real-only training. - Report impact on minority-class metrics, especially Recall_pinkeye and F1_pinkeye.

Goal: - Improve robustness and class balance by augmenting limited real pink-eye samples with high-quality synthetic data.

7) Support Needed: Synthetic Data Curation

After synthetic images are generated, I will need support for a data-curation pass before using them in model training.

Reason: - The generated samples are not expected to be 100% correct. - Some images may contain visual artifacts, unrealistic anatomy, or incorrect class appearance.

Requested support: - Help review synthetic image batches and remove low-quality/incorrect samples. - Help maintain a cleaned subset of synthetic data for training experiments. - Optionally define a simple curation rubric to keep filtering consistent across reviewers.

Expected impact: - Higher quality augmented dataset. - Lower risk of introducing noisy labels or harmful artifacts into classifier training. - More reliable benchmark comparisons after augmentation.
